comment: Self-absorbed man, constantly references that he is the ex-president. You end up doing his own pet projects for class and there is no clear course material or design. I can confidently say I didn't gain as much from this course as I would have another FYS.

Dr. Ayers did a fine job of guiding his FYS students toward an interesting final product - a website for the museum. He is a great guy and takes a personal interest in his students as people. However, the class was generally really unfocused and not exactly what everyone signed up for.

He makes you do his grunt work for his class, probably projects he's always wanted to do, but never got around to doing it since he was president of the University. Most of his classes are just him talking about the website he wants to make for a museum and some classes there really isn't a point of going; no one, not even him, speaks in class.

Dr. Ayers is a fabulous professor, and I felt so fortunate to have a place in his first freshman class at UR.  His expectations may be high, but I gained and learned so much in his class.  By far one of my all-time favorite professors!
He really is a great teacher. I feel fortunate having him.

this is one overrated guy. always said he hated admin, and became an administrator... a man with a great *scholarly* future behind him -and not really a nice man in the end at all; he is vicious and vain if provoked; theoretically wanting
Great lecturer!  Lousy TAs!!!  Slavery is an emotion topic.  Be prepared to do a ton of research!  This is why I gave it a 1 for easiness.  Good Luck!
i don't understand what all the hype is about

Ayers is hands down the best professor at the University.  His passion is unrivaled while his intelligence is unparalleled.  No matter which department you are in, take Ayers' course for a true Jeffersonian collegiate experience.
Very dedicated and enthusiastic professor.  A MUST for any history major.  You'll kick yourself if you don't take one of his classes while at the university.
Best class I've taken at UVA.  Not a gut though.
Ayers' lectures are worthwhile and make you proud that you attended UVA.  To bad class is mostly controlled by TAs.  Not easy class, but if you enjoy history, take this class.
No Comments
Ayers is sexy, smart, funny, and an AWESOME lecturer.  His class, Rise and Fall of the Slave South, is a MUST TAKE at UVA!  Although it isn't an incredibly easy class, it's still worth it!!

If you have the opportunity to take his class do it. If you do not have the opportunity to take his class, take the time to go to some lectures. His lectures are like a baptist sermon. He loves what he does and you will too.
Probably the best lecturer on grounds. TA's were weak but hey...wish I could have had this prof leading the section.

I took this class my first year...Ayers is the best.  He's dynamic, passionate, and charismatic...he could tell you anything you want to know about Southern history and culture.  Not mention, he's pretty damn sexy when he lectures.
TAKE THIS CLASS.  Every girl falls in love with him, but he is phenomenal.  He lives up to the hype.  Elzinga's class is not the "must take" class of UVA, this (and Bond's class) is.
funny and entertaining undergrad, a bit narrow grad if you're not of his school, but he'll fight for you. much overrated in new teaching concepts, but by now a UVa experience.
Da Dean is Da Bomb.
He is absolutely phenomenal! Incredibly dynamic, interesting, funny, and brilliant. Any course with him is bound to be amazing!
Ayers is a dynamic professor, who is funny and knows his history of the American South.
